coverage_note: Municipal police officers and firefighters under the Fire and Police Arbitration Act, 11 O.S. 51-101 et seq. The Municipal Employee Collective Bargaining Act (51-200 to 51-220) was repealed in 2011, and no statute captured gives State or other local employees bargaining rights. Source caveat: OSCN is behind a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge and oklegislature.gov disallows all crawling in robots.txt, so the text is the Oklahoma Senate's copy of Title 11 uploaded May 2022. That copy still shows the Public Employees Relations Board; later changes to the board and election procedure (reportedly 2019 H.B. 1968) were not verified, so the board and unfair-labor-practice cells are null.

governing_statute.value: Fire and Police Arbitration Act, 11 O.S. 51-101 to 51-113 (municipal police and firefighters only)
governing_statute.quote: A. Firefighters and police officers in any municipality shall have the separate right to bargain collectively with their municipality and to be represented by a bargaining agent in such collective bargaining

who_may_bargain.value: Permanent members of paid municipal fire and police departments. Non-uniformed municipal employees lost statutory bargaining when the Municipal Employee Collective Bargaining Act was repealed in 2011.
who_may_bargain.quote: It is declared to be the public policy of this state to accord to the permanent members of any paid fire department or police department in any municipality all of the rights of labor, other than the right to strike or to engage in any work stoppage or slowdown.

impasse_procedure.value: If no agreement within 30 days of the first meeting, either party may demand arbitration by a three-member board that must pick one side's last best offer. If the city's offer is not selected, the city may put both offers to the voters at a special election.
impasse_procedure.quote: a majority of the arbitration board members shall select one of the two last best offers as the contract of the parties.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited for municipal police and firefighters. No statute captured addresses other public employees.
strike_legality.quote: Nothing in this article shall constitute a grant of the right to strike to fire fighters or police officers of any municipality and such strikes are hereby prohibited.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018). Oklahoma's right-to-work provision was not captured for this row.
